mechanism_narrative: Consistent month-over-month growth in housing starts (HOUST) signals robust consumer demand for residential construction, which typically precedes stronger corporate earnings and positive equity market sentiment, driving S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained federal funds rate increases above 5.0% for three consecutive months signal aggressive monetary tightening, which compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates and reduced liquidity, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates tightening monetary policy during labor market strength, triggering recession fears and reduced corporate profitability that drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening cycle with strong labor market
failure_condition: The joint effect of rising FEDFUNDS and falling UNRATE does not produce negative returns in more than 60% of instances, as measured by Rank IC < -0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) during late-cycle contraction regimes (defined by GDPC1 growth < 1.5% and UNRATE < 4.5%) signals weakening supply chain activity and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the late-cycle contraction regime condition (GDPC1 growth < 1.5% and UNRATE < 4.5%) when INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: Steady month-over-month growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.3% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: Real sales of new single-family homes (RSAFS) exceeding $700 billion reflect strong consumer demand for housing, which typically boosts economic growth and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 700000.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% and remaining elevated for two months), the S&P 500 declines as higher interest rates pressure equity valuations and economic growth, resulting in negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the monetary tightening cycle condition (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 2 consecutive months).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates demand-supply misalignment that creates inflationary pressures and market uncertainty, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of rising HOUST and falling INDPRO does not produce negative returns in more than 60% of instances, as measured by Rank IC < -0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
